gf001.e: を marks the direct object: パンを たべる.

gf002.e: で marks the place where an action happens.
gf002.t: I get on the train at the station.

gf003.e: へ (or に) shows direction: にほんへ いく.
gf003.t: I'm going to Japan next year.

gf004.t: I get up at 7 every day.

gf005.t: I went to see a movie with a friend.

gf006.e: 〜に もらう: to receive from someone (から also works).
gf006.t: I got this bag from my mother.

gf008.e: 〜が あります: there is. The subject takes が.
gf008.t: There is a book on the desk.

gf009.e: すき/きらい/じょうず take が.

gf012.e: A と B: A and B (complete list).

gf013.e: や…など: A, B, and so on (incomplete list).
gf013.t: In the room there are a desk, chairs, and so on.

gf014.e: A と B と どちらが: which do you prefer, A or B?
gf014.t: Which do you like better, coffee or tea?

gf015.e: A は B より: A is more… than B.
gf015.t: My older brother is taller than me.

gf016.e: 〜の なかで いちばん: the most… among.
gf016.t: Of all fruits, which do you like best?

gf017.t: Both Tanaka and Yamada are students.

gf018.e: ね seeks agreement; the reply そうですね confirms it.
gf018.t: "This book is interesting, isn't it?" "Yes, it is."

gf019.e: よ: giving information the listener doesn't know.
gf019.t: "Is there a test tomorrow?" "Yes, there is."

gf020.e: ぐらい: about (amounts, durations). ごろ is for points in time.
gf020.t: It takes about 10 minutes to walk to the station.

gf021.e: ごろ: around (an approximate time): 11じごろに.
gf021.t: Yesterday I went to bed around 11.

gf023.e: だけ (with an affirmative verb): only.

gf024.t: There is nobody in the room.

gf025.t: I didn't go anywhere on Sunday.

gf027.e: 〜で はたらく: to work at (place of the action).

gf028.t: My younger sister lives in Tokyo.

gf029.e: に: the place where something is written/put.

gf030.e: を with verbs of moving through a place: こうえんを さんぽする.
gf030.t: I take walks in this park.

gf031.e: かどを まがる: to turn at the corner.
gf031.t: Please turn right at the next corner.

gf032.e: 〜を おりる: to get off.
gf032.t: I got off the bus and walked a little.

gf035.t: I wrote a letter in Japanese.

gf038.e: ます-stem + に いく: to go to do something.
gf038.t: I'm going to the library to return a book.

gf039.e: なにを しに: to do what?
gf039.t: What did you come to Japan for?

gf040.t: "Would you like to have lunch together?" "Sure, let's eat."

gf041.t: We're a little tired, aren't we? Let's rest here.

gf042.t: I went to the department store yesterday, but I didn't buy anything.

gf043.e: ます-stem + たい: to want to do.
gf043.t: I'm thirsty. I want to drink some water.

gf044.e: 〜て います: action in progress.

gf046.e: 〜ても いいですか: may I…?
gf046.t: Excuse me, may I use this pen?

gf047.e: 〜ては いけません: it is forbidden.

gf048.e: 〜ないで ください: please don't…
gf048.t: It's dangerous, so please don't swim in this river.

gf049.t: I wash my hands and then eat.

gf050.t: I brush my teeth before going to bed.

gf051.t: Please take the medicine after meals.

gf052.t: I do my homework while listening to music.

gf053.e: 〜たり 〜たり する: doing things like…
gf053.t: On Sundays I do things like cleaning and laundry.

gf054.e: na-adjective + に する: to make something…

gf055.e: i-adjective + なる: さむい → さむく なる.
gf055.t: It suddenly got cold since yesterday, didn't it?

gf056.e: noun + に なる: to become.
gf056.t: My younger sister will become a student next year.

gf057.e: Linking an i-adjective: ひろくて.
gf057.t: This room is spacious and bright.

gf058.e: Linking a na-adjective: しずかで.
gf058.t: This town is quiet and pretty.

gf059.e: Past of an i-adjective: さむかったです.

gf060.e: Past of a na-adjective: かんたんでした.

gf061.e: Negative of an i-adjective: おいしくないです.

gf062.e: Negative of a na-adjective: きれいじゃ ありません.

gf063.t: The weather is nice, so let's go for a walk.

gf064.t: This room is spacious, but a little dark.

gf065.e: Answering どうして: 〜からです.
gf065.t: "Why were you absent?" "Because I had a headache."

gf066.e: しって いますか: do you know? (しる is always 〜て いる here).
gf066.t: Do you know the meaning of this word?

gf067.e: Negative answer: しりません (not しって いません).
gf067.t: "Do you know the meaning of this word?" "No, I don't."

gf068.e: もつ → もって いる: to have.
gf068.t: My older brother has two cars.

gf069.e: 〜た ことが ある: to have done something before.

gf070.t: When I was a child, I often played in this park.

gf071.t: When you cross the road, please watch out for cars.

gf072.t: "Did you go anywhere during the summer holidays?" "No, I didn't go anywhere."

gf074.t: "Did you eat anything?" "No, I didn't eat anything."

gf075.e: A hobby is expressed with こと: 本を よむ ことです.

gf076.e: 〜のが すき: to like doing something.

gf077.e: いくらですか: how much is it?

gf078.e: なんで (by what means): バスで.
gf078.t: "How do you get to the station?" "I go by bus."

gf080.t: "Where did you study Japanese?" "I studied it at university."

gf081.e: だれのですか: whose is it?

gf082.e: どれ: which one (pronoun). どの needs a noun after it.
gf082.t: "Which one is Yamada's bag?" "That black bag over there."

gf083.t: "Which person is Tanaka?" "That tall person over there."

gf084.e: どうですか: how is it?
gf084.t: "How is life in Japan?" "It's a lot of fun."

gf085.e: どんな + noun: what kind of.
gf085.t: "What kind of person is Tanaka?" "A kind person."

gf086.t: "How many apples did you buy?" "I bought five."

gf087.e: なんにん: how many people.
gf087.t: "How many people are in your family?" "Four."

gf088.t: "How did you get here?" "I came by taxi."

gf089.e: なんじまで: until what time?

gf090.e: A も B も: both A and B.
gf090.t: Tanaka can speak both English and Chinese.

gf091.e: 〜に あります: to be in/at (a place).
gf091.t: My room is on the second floor.

gf092.t: There's no milk in the fridge.

gf093.t: Tanaka is in the meeting room now.

gf094.e: Place of an action (あそぶ): で.
gf094.t: Children are playing in the park.

gf096.t: Which is faster, the train or the bus? The train is faster.

gf097.t: What time of year do you like best?

gf098.e: 〜た ほうが いい: you'd better…
gf098.t: This question is difficult, so you'd better ask the teacher.

gf099.e: dictionary form + つもり: to intend to. (N5/N4.)
gf099.t: I plan to go back to my country during the summer holidays.

gf100.e: 〜なければ なりません: must, have to.
gf100.t: I have to go home early today.

gf101.e: 〜なくても いい: you don't have to.
gf101.t: There's no school tomorrow, so you don't have to get up early.

gf103.e: あいて いる (intransitive): is open.
gf103.t: The window is open. Who opened it?

gf104.t: Please close the door. It's cold.

gf105.e: ついて いる: to be on (intransitive).
gf105.t: The light is on, even though nobody is here.

gf106.e: Tricky one (N4): transitive + て あります, the resulting state of a deliberate action.
gf106.t: A calendar has been put up on the wall.

gf107.t: There's no time, so please hurry.

gf108.e: まって ください: please wait.
gf108.t: Excuse me, please wait a moment.

gf109.e: 〜て くださいませんか: very polite request.
gf109.t: Could you please speak a little more slowly?

gf110.e: まだ 〜て いません: not yet.
gf110.t: "Have you had lunch yet?" "No, I haven't eaten yet."

gf111.t: "Have you finished your homework yet?" "Yes, I've already finished."

gf112.e: Past: きのう → おきました.
gf112.t: I get up at 6 every morning. But yesterday I got up at 8.

gf113.t: The child is sleeping, so please be quiet.

gf114.e: i-adjective + する: あまく する.
gf114.t: This soup was a little spicy, so I added some sugar to make it sweeter.

gf115.t: Tanaka went back to his country last week.

gf116.e: きょねん → past: あつかったです.
gf116.t: Last summer was very hot, wasn't it?

gf117.e: End of the sentence: i-adjective + です.
gf117.t: The ramen at this shop is cheap and tasty.

gf118.e: With 〜たい you can use を or が; here only を is among the valid options.
gf118.t: I want to buy a new car.

gf119.t: Every night I write in my diary before going to bed.

gf120.e: Tricky one (N4): ます-stem + やすい, easy to use.
gf120.t: This camera is easy to use.

gf121.t: It's raining, so I'm not going anywhere today.

gf122.e: 〜た ほうが いい: advice.
gf122.t: It's cold at the top of the mountain, so you'd better take a sweater.

gf123.e: At a library you borrow (かりる).
gf123.t: I borrowed this book from the library.

gf124.e: Someone gives to me: くれる.
gf124.t: A friend gave me flowers on my birthday.

gf125.e: I give to someone else: あげる.
gf125.t: I gave a book to my younger brother.

gf126.e: 〜から もらう: to receive from.
gf126.t: I received a dictionary from my teacher.

gf127.t: It's already been two years since I came to Japan.

gf128.e: Negative na-adjective: じょうずでは ありません.
gf128.t: I'm not good at Japanese yet.

gf129.e: Noun in the past: あめでした.

gf130.e: 〜ふん まえ: five minutes to (five to nine).
gf130.t: What time is it now? It's five to nine.

gf131.e: Tricky one (N4): 〜と, if you go straight, the bank appears.
gf131.t: If you go straight along this road, there's a bank on the left.

gf132.e: ぐらい: approximate duration. ごろ is for a specific point in time.
gf132.t: My older brother watches about two hours of TV every night.

gf133.t: "Excuse me, where is the post office?" "It's behind that building."

gf134.t: From Tokyo to Osaka it's three hours by shinkansen.

gf135.e: Future with a noun: しごとです.
gf135.t: Today is a day off, but tomorrow I have work.

gf136.e: 〜に する: to decide on, choose.
gf136.t: "What will you drink?" "I'll have black tea."

gf137.e: Chaining actions: たべて, いきます.
gf137.t: Every day I eat breakfast and go to school.

gf138.e: dictionary form + まえに: before coming.
gf138.t: Before coming to Japan, I studied a little Japanese.

gf139.t: This is a cake my mother made. It's very delicious.

gf140.t: "How was that movie?" "It wasn't very interesting."

gf141.t: I don't like meat. But I like fish.

gf142.e: それから: and also, and then.
gf142.t: Yesterday I bought a shirt at the department store. I also bought shoes.

gf143.t: It was raining a lot. So I didn't go anywhere.

gf144.e: 〜では ありません: is not.
gf144.t: "Is that person Tanaka?" "No, it isn't Tanaka."

gf145.t: This room is spacious, but not very bright.

gf146.t: Before tests, I study three hours every day.

gf147.e: しりませんでした: didn't know either.
gf147.t: I asked the teacher, but the teacher didn't know either.

gf148.t: Would you like to go see a movie together this Sunday?

gf149.t: It's a bit hot, isn't it? Shall I open the window?

gf150.e: 〜ましょうか: shall I carry it for you?
gf150.t: "Your luggage looks heavy. Shall I carry it?" "Thank you very much."

gf151.e: までに: by (a deadline). まで shows a continuous duration.
gf151.t: Please return this book by Friday.

gf152.e: 〜に いる: to be at home.
gf152.t: On my days off I'm always at home.

gf153.e: できました: has opened (was built).
gf153.t: A new shop has opened in front of the station.

gf154.e: Indirect question: どう よむか わからない.
gf154.t: I don't know how to read this kanji.

gf155.e: 〜か どうか: whether or not.
gf155.t: "Is Tanaka coming?" "Hmm, I don't know whether he's coming or not."

gf156.e: 〜が いちばん: … is the best.
gf156.t: On hot days, a cold beer tastes best.

gf157.e: Answering どちら: 〜の ほうが.
gf157.t: "Who is younger, Tanaka or Yamada?" "Yamada is younger."

gf158.e: 〜ことが できる: to be able to.

gf159.e: Tricky one (N4): ように して いる, to make a habit of.
gf159.t: I make a point of running in the park for about 30 minutes every morning.

gf160.t: It's gotten dark, so let's go home now.

gf161.t: Please don't go into the room.

gf162.t: My younger sister is good at singing.

gf163.e: People: いる. いま → present.
gf163.t: My father is at the office now.

gf164.t: There is a big tree in the park.

gf165.t: There are two cats in the garden.

gf166.t: Where is the book you bought yesterday?

gf167.t: I like dogs, but I don't like cats.

gf168.t: Yesterday I went to visit a friend's house.

gf169.t: On rainy days I do things like reading books and listening to music at home.

gf170.t: In Hokkaido, it gets very cold when winter comes.

gf171.t: After graduating from university, I went to work for a bank.

gf172.e: Past of the i-adjective つまらない: つまらなかったです.
gf172.t: Tanaka's talk was long and boring.

gf174.e: Description: かみが ながい.
gf174.t: Yamada is tall and has long hair.

gf175.e: ひとりでは できない: can't be done alone.
gf175.t: This work can't be done by one person alone.

gf176.t: My older brother goes to work by bicycle.

gf177.t: How long does it take from your house to the station?

gf178.e: どう しましたか: what's wrong?
gf178.t: "You don't look well. What's wrong?" "I have a bit of a headache."

gf179.e: Tricky one: ひとつで 100えん, 100 yen apiece.

gf180.e: なにを たべましたか.
gf180.t: What did you have for dinner last night?

gf181.e: 〜に とまる: to stop at.
gf181.t: Does this train stop at Tokyo Station?

gf182.t: "Why were you absent from school yesterday?" "Because I had a fever."

gf183.t: I read a Japanese newspaper every day.

gf184.e: けっこんして いる: to be married.

gf185.t: This is the book I borrowed from the library last week.

gf186.t: Vegetables are cheap in summer, but expensive in winter.

gf187.e: くる まえに: before (they) come.
gf187.t: I cleaned my room before my friend came.

gf188.t: After watching the movie, we had a meal at a restaurant.

gf189.e: Tricky one (N4): 〜たら, if it rains.
gf189.t: If it rains, there will be no game.

gf190.e: どちらでも いい: either one is fine.
gf190.t: "Which would you like, coffee or tea?" "Either is fine."

gf191.t: My house is close to the station, so it's convenient.

gf192.e: Tricky one (N4): adj + すぎる, too big.
gf192.t: The shoes I bought yesterday are a little too big.

gf194.t: Last year, in Japan, I saw Mt. Fuji for the first time.

gf195.e: 〜て くれませんか: could you…?
gf195.t: Could you say it once more?

gf196.t: There's only one tall building in my town.

gf198.e: Tricky one: でも, "something cold, for example".
gf198.t: It's hot, isn't it? Let's have something cold to drink or something.

gf199.t: My younger brother turned twenty this year.

gf200.e: A も B も すき: I like both A and B.
gf200.t: I like both dogs and cats.

gf201.t: I listen to music every night.

gf204.e: Tricky one: こうえんを はしる (running through). で is also used, but it isn't among the options.
gf204.t: My older brother runs in the park every morning.

gf205.t: Does this train go to Tokyo?

gf206.e: ひとつも + negative: not even one.
gf206.t: I don't know a single Japanese song.

gf207.e: しか + negative: there's only a TV.
gf207.t: There's only a TV in the room.

gf208.t: Yesterday I showed my composition to the teacher.

gf210.t: I'll wait for my friend in front of the station.

gf212.t: My younger sister is good at singing.

gf213.t: I was absent from school because I was sick.

gf214.e: ふたりで: the two of us together.
gf214.t: The two of us went to see a movie.

gf215.e: さんぼんで: for three in total.
gf215.t: This pen is 100 yen each. Three of them are 300 yen.

gf217.t: I work about eight hours every day.

gf218.t: "Who did you hear that story from?" "From Yamada."

gf219.t: From here to the station is a five-minute walk.

gf220.t: The summer holidays last until August 31st.

gf221.t: My house is close to the school.

gf223.e: A か B か: A or B?
gf223.t: Will you have coffee or tea?

gf224.t: If it rains tomorrow, I won't go.

gf225.t: Please turn off the light when you leave the room.

gf226.t: I have never made Japanese food yet.

gf227.t: Last week I ate sushi for the first time.

gf228.t: We have time, so let's walk there.

gf229.t: That person can speak English, but can't speak Japanese.

gf230.t: I put on my glasses to read the newspaper.

gf231.t: Since coming to Japan, my Japanese has gotten a little better.

gf232.t: This room is dark, so please make it brighter.

gf233.t: Today it's neither hot nor cold.

gf235.e: Tricky one (N4): あいだに, while.
gf235.t: While the child was sleeping, I cleaned up.

gf236.t: The rain has stopped. Shall we go for a walk?

gf237.e: まだ + いる: is still there.
gf237.t: Has Tanaka gone home yet? No, he's still at the office.

gf238.t: I want a cold drink. Is there anything?

gf239.t: Who did you give the book you bought yesterday to?

gf240.e: Indirect question: 〜か わからない.
gf240.t: I don't know what time the meeting will end.

gf241.t: On snowy days, you'd better not drive.

gf242.t: Please take this medicine before going to bed.

gf243.t: "Shall we go home together?" "Sorry, I still have work to do."

gf244.t: The weather was nice, so I did the laundry.

gf245.t: This question is difficult, and I don't understand it at all.

gf246.e: I called, but she didn't answer.
gf246.t: I called my mother, but she didn't answer.

gf247.e: かって いる: to keep (a pet).

gf248.e: Tricky one: intransitive + て いる (state).
gf248.t: There's a clock hanging on the wall.

gf249.t: I overslept and didn't make it in time for the train.

gf250.t: After I graduate from university, I plan to go back to my country.

gf251.t: It's hot, isn't it? May I open the window?

gf252.t: You must not talk loudly in the library.

gf253.t: Tomorrow is a day off, so I don't have to get up early.

gf254.t: Before the test I have to study a lot.

gf256.t: Yamada is tall, and he also has long legs.

gf257.t: Tokyo has more people than Osaka.

gf258.e: Tricky one (N4): 〜ほど 〜ない, not as… as.
gf258.t: Osaka doesn't have as many people as Tokyo.

gf259.e: いちばん すきです.
gf259.t: Of all the seasons, I like spring best.

gf260.t: This is a photo I took.

gf261.t: I didn't really understand what the teacher said.

gf262.t: I'm tired, so let's rest a little.

gf263.t: I walk while listening to music.

gf264.t: Let's wash our hands before eating.

gf265.t: After I finish my homework, I watch TV.

gf266.t: In my free time I do things like reading books and watching movies.

gf267.e: AとB: A and B (パンと 牛乳).
gf267.t: My breakfast is always bread and milk.

gf268.t: "Would you like something to drink?" "Well then, juice, please."

gf269.t: I lost the watch I got from my father.

gf270.t: I'm going to the airport to pick up a friend.
